title: Tate twists preserve supports of cohomology sheaves
statement: Let $X$ be a separated scheme of finite type over the field $k$ of [def-per-support-condition], let $M\in D^b_c(X,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell)$ be an object of the bounded constructible $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$-coefficient category of [def-weil-pbc-qbar-category], and let $m\in\mathbf Z$. Let $M(m)=M\otimes^L\overline{\mathbf Q}_{\ell,X}(m)$ be its Tate twist as in [def-coefficient-twists-detailed]. Then $M(m)\in D^b_c(X,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell)$, and for every integer $a$ there is a natural isomorphism of cohomology sheaves [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves] $\mathcal H^a(M(m))\cong\mathcal H^a(M)\otimes\overline{\mathbf Q}_{\ell,X}(m)$, whose fibre at every geometric point $\bar x$ of $X$ is $\mathcal H^a(M)_{\bar x}\otimes_{\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell}L_{\bar x}$ with $L_{\bar x}$ a one-dimensional $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$-vector space. In particular $\operatorname{Supp}\mathcal H^a(M(m))=\operatorname{Supp}\mathcal H^a(M)$ for every $a$, and with the support condition of [def-per-support-condition], $\operatorname{SuppCon}(M)$ holds if and only if $\operatorname{SuppCon}(M(m))$ holds.

source.place: second paragraph: 'The twist $(d)$ is lisse of rank one, hence support-preserving'

proof.text: Put $L=\overline{\mathbf Q}_{\ell,X}(m)$. The scheme $X$ is separated of finite type over a field, hence noetherian of finite dimension, and $\ell$ is invertible on $X$ because $D^b_c(X,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell)$ of [def-weil-pbc-qbar-category] is defined only for such schemes. By [lem-per-tate-twist-lisse-line] (clauses 1 and 2), $L$ is, in degree zero, the lisse $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$-sheaf $\mathcal T$ of rank one in the adic sense, with one-dimensional fibre $\mathcal T_{\bar x}=L_{\bar x}$ at every geometric point, and by its clause 3 the twist $M(m)$ of [def-coefficient-twists-detailed] is naturally isomorphic to $M\otimes^L\mathcal T$ formed with the completed operations. Apply [lem-per-adic-lisse-cohomology-calculus] to $K=M$ and $\mathcal L=\mathcal T$. It gives $M\otimes^L\mathcal T\in D^b_c(X,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell)$, hence $M(m)\in D^b_c(X,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell)$, and, for every $a$, a natural isomorphism $\mathcal H^a(M(m))\cong\mathcal H^a(M)\otimes L$, whose geometric-point fibre is $\mathcal H^a(M)_{\bar x}\otimes_{\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell}L_{\bar x}$ with $L_{\bar x}$ one-dimensional.

source.place: second paragraph, first sentence: the twist is lisse of rank one

proof.text: For any geometric point $\bar x$, tensoring a $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$-vector space with the one-dimensional space $L_{\bar x}$ is an isomorphism onto a vector space of the same dimension, and it is zero exactly when the original vector space is zero. The fibre description in Step 1 therefore gives, for every $a$, equality of the loci where the stalks of $\mathcal H^a(M(m))$ and $\mathcal H^a(M)$ are nonzero. Taking closures in the definition of support yields $\operatorname{Supp}\mathcal H^a(M(m))=\operatorname{Supp}\mathcal H^a(M)$.

The support condition [def-per-support-condition] is a conjunction of dimension inequalities for these supports. Since Step 2 gives equality for every cohomological index, all its inequalities hold for $M$ exactly when they hold for $M(m)$. Thus $\operatorname{SuppCon}(M)$ holds if and only if $\operatorname{SuppCon}(M(m))$ holds.
